# Thinking it through — this year's plan

Aiya, another year. I've been working these 6 mu for over forty years now, since I married into this village. My eyes aren't what they were, and my back hurts in the morning, but the land doesn't farm itself. Two of my sons are in Handan city doing construction, my daughter's married out, and my daughter-in-law helps on weekends when she's not at the factory. So most days it's me out there with my grandson when he's not in school.

**Splitting the fields.** I'll do it the way I did last year — 2 mu of garlic near the house, 4 mu of wheat further out. The garlic makes better money than wheat if the price holds, but it's hard work, bending over to plant the cloves one by one, and the harvest in May breaks your back. Two mu is all I can manage. Any more and I'd have to hire too many people. The wheat on the other 4 mu is easier — old Wang down the road brings his rototiller and the combine comes through in June, I just pay for the service. After I pull the garlic in May, that ground goes to maize. After wheat comes off in June, that ground also goes to maize. So in summer all 6 mu is maize.

**Seed.** For garlic I save my own seed cloves from last year's best bulbs — buying seed garlic is 600-700 yuan per mu, too expensive. For wheat I buy Jimai or whatever variety the agro-shop has, about 8 yuan per jin. For maize I buy hybrid seed, Zhengdan or Xianyu, whatever my neighbors say did well.

**Fertilizer.** I don't measure precisely like those university people. For garlic I put down 3 bags of the 15-15-15 compound before planting, then topdress with urea in March when it starts growing — maybe half a bag per mu. Garlic is greedy, if you don't feed it the bulbs stay small. For wheat, 2 bags of compound at planting, then urea at jointing, maybe 15 kg per mu. For maize, I put a little compound in with the seed and topdress urea when it's knee-high. I use a bit more than my neighbor because the one year I cut back the wheat came out yellow and thin — not going to make that mistake again.

**Water.** The well is shared with three other households. Garlic gets watered 4 times through winter and spring — once after planting, once before winter, once in spring when it wakes up, once before the bulbs swell. Wheat gets 3 times usually — after planting if dry, before winter, and at jointing. Maize I try to get by with one watering, unless July-August is dry like 2022 when I had to water twice.

**Pesticide.** Garlic rust is the worst problem, I spray 2-3 times. Also onion maggots when I see them. Wheat I spray once for aphids and rust together. Maize usually just one herbicide spray early — pests aren't usually bad here.

**Money.** This is the part that worries me. Garlic is expensive to grow — maybe 1500 yuan per mu in inputs if I save my own seed. Wheat and maize together maybe 800 yuan per mu for the pair. Total for the year will be around 7000-8000 yuan. If the garlic price is decent — last year was 3.5 yuan per jin dried — I'll make some money. If it crashes like 2019, aiya, we'll be tight.

Here's my plan:
